B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year was Plutonium discovered?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
In what year was Tungsten discovered?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
Ilyushin Il-96: Voronezh Aircraft Production Association. It is powered by four high-bypass Aviadvigatel PS-90 twin-spool turbofan engines.
Which country is AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo from?
AIDC F-CK-1 Ching-kuo: Taiwan. The aircraft made its first flight in 1989.
Who is credited with discovering Xenon?
Xenon: William Ramsay. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Who is credited with discovering RDX?
RDX: Georg Friedrich Henning. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Who is credited with discovering Aluminium?
Aluminium: Hans Christian Ørsted. Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
Once thought to be the last living species in its genus after a related 'sea' cousin went extinct, this North American mustelid now thrives as an invasive species in Europe — which animal?
American mink (Neogale vison) is a semiaquatic species of mustelid native to North America, though human introduction has expanded its range to many parts of Europe, Asia, and South America.
Sharing the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics with Martin Ryle for the discovery of pulsars, which British radio astronomer had already earned the Royal Astronomical Society's Eddington Medal in 1969?

Antony Hewish (11 May 1924 - 13 September 2021) was a British radio astronomer who won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1974 (together with fellow radio-astronomer Martin Ryle) for his role in the discovery of pulsars.

A professor at the University of North Carolina, this molecular biologist co-founded a foundation supporting Turkish students while researching DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, and circadian rhythms — who is he?
Aziz Sancar (born 8 September 1946) is a Turkish-American molecular biologist specializing in DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, and circadian clock.
From molecules and cells up to whole ecosystems, this science studies living things through ideas like heredity, evolution, and homeostasis — what is it?
Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.
Named in a 2018 New York Times essay by Bari Weiss as part of the 'intellectual dark web,' this former evolutionary biology professor left academia after 2017 campus protests — who is he?
Bret Weinstein (born February 21, 1969) is an American podcaster, author, and former professor of evolutionary biology.

Ranging from 9 to 20 centimeters long and known on the Italian mainland by a slightly different name, this Sicilian pastry features a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with a sweet ricotta cream — which pastry?
Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
This genus of deciduous trees and shrubs in the beech family, native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, gives its name to a widely eaten edible nut it produces — what's this tree (and nut) called?
Chestnut are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.
Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.

Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flesh,' this breakdown product of muscle and protein metabolism is released into the bloodstream at a rate depending on a person's muscle mass — name the substance?
Creatinine (from Ancient Greek (kras) 'flesh') is a breakdown product of creatine phosphate from muscle and protein metabolism.
This biological process breaks down large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components for absorption into the bloodstream, via both mechanical and chemical means. What is it?
Digestion is the breakdown of large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components so that they can be absorbed into the blood plasma.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints, stretchy velvety skin, and abnormal scarring, sometimes leading to aortic dissection — name the condition?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) are a group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders.
This flammable, colorless solvent smells sweetly of pear drops and shows up in glues and nail polish remover — and it's also the ester used to gently strip caffeine from tea and coffee. What is it?
Ethyl acetate (commonly abbreviated EtOAc or EA) is the organic compound with the formula CH3CO2CH2CH3, simplified to C4H8O2.

Also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome after the pair of psychiatrists who first described it, this shared delusional disorder is named for the small number of people who typically experience it together — what is it called?

Folie à deux (French for 'madness of two'), also called shared psychosis or shared delusional disorder (SDD), is a rare psychiatric syndrome in which symptoms of a delusional belief are "transmitted" from one individual to another.
Nicknamed 'The Lawyer' and celebrated for his eccentric style, this principal shareholder controlled over 4% of Italy's entire GDP through his automaker — who was he?
Gianni Agnelli (12 March 1921 - 24 January 2003), nicknamed L'Avvocato ('The Lawyer'), was an Italian industrialist and principal shareholder of Fiat.
This eel-shaped ocean scavenger defends itself by flooding predators with slime from glands in its skin — what creature is it?
Hagfish (also known as Hyperotreti) and order Myxiniformes, are eel-shaped jawless fish (occasionally called slime eels).
Also called the ratel, this animal is Africa's largest land-dwelling mustelid, armed with remarkably loose skin that lets it twist around and bite back even when grabbed. What is it?
Honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel (or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
Its partial form is called 'subileus' — this condition describes an intestine that can't propel its contents forward, whether from a lack of peristalsis or a mechanical blockage — what is it?
Ileus is a disruption of the normal propulsive ability of the intestine.
This German-American software engineer designed PayPal's real-time anti-fraud system, then co-founded a site whose very first video — "Me at the zoo" — he uploaded himself in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim (born October 28, 1979) is a German and American software engineer and internet entrepreneur.
This Afghan-American author sought asylum in the U.S. as a teenager and later wrote a bestselling debut novel set in his homeland before working as a UNHCR goodwill ambassador — who is he?
Khaled Hosseini (Pashto/; born March 4, 1965) is an Afghan and American novelist, UNHCR goodwill ambassador, and former physician.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.

With only six species left today, spread across Africa, South America, and Australia, this ancient group's fossil record stretches back over 410 million years to the Early Devonian — what group is it?
Lungfish are freshwater vertebrates belonging to the class Dipnoi.

Encompassing complex, functional, and measure theory as major subfields, this branch of mathematics studies real numbers, sequences, series, and limits with rigor formalized in the 19th century — which field?
Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This Soviet tandem-seat helicopter was built purely for anti-armor attack missions, carrying no secondary transport capacity unlike the gunship it succeeded — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

This condition, an inflammation of the heart muscle itself, can cause shortness of breath, chest pain, and irregular heartbeat, and may progress to heart failure if it leads to chronic remodeling of the heart — name the condition?

Myocarditis is inflammation of the cardiac muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
Containing turbinates and olfactory mucosa within its cavity, this organ centers the human face and provides an alternate airway while infants nurse — which body part?
Nose is a sensory organ and respiratory structure in vertebrates.
Also called trioxygen and far less stable than the oxygen we breathe, it carries the formula O3 and smells faintly of chlorine — what is this gas?
Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3.
Sprayed on clothing and mosquito nets or applied as a cream against lice and scabies, this pyrethroid discovered in 1972 is highly toxic to fish and to cats — what is it?
Permethrin is a medication and an insecticide.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.
This viscous, nearly odorless liquid with a faintly sweet taste is classified as a diol and is approved by the FDA as a safe food additive — what compound is it?
Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
This transhumanist inventor who pioneered text-to-speech and OCR technology later won the $500,000 Lemelson-MIT Prize in 2001 for his work on artificial intelligence — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil (born February 12, 1948) is an American computer scientist, author, entrepreneur, futurist, and inventor.
Born in 1858, this German inventor devised a compression-ignition engine so significant that it and its fuel now both carry his surname — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel (18 March 1858 - 29 September 1913) was a German inventor and mechanical engineer.

This potentially life-threatening condition occurs when the body's dysregulated response to infection damages its own tissues and organs, often causing fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — what is it called?
Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Called sun spiders, camel spiders, and wind scorpions, these dry-climate arachnids are neither true spiders nor scorpions, and urban legends wildly exaggerate their danger — what order are they?
Solifugae is an order of arachnids known variously as solifuges, sun spiders, camel spiders, wind scorpions, and jerrymanders.
This artificial sweetener is produced by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and is roughly 600 times sweeter than sucrose — three times sweeter even than aspartame — what's the sweetener called?

Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and sugar substitute. The commercial success of sucralose-based products stems from its favorable comparison to other low-calorie sweeteners in terms of taste, stability, and safety.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Latin for 'three-headed,' this large muscle on the back of the upper arm has three parts, one of which also crosses the shoulder joint — name the muscle?
Triceps (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.

Native to Europe and parts of Asia, this parasitic plant draws water and nutrients from host trees and has long featured in European mythology, now commonly used in Christmas decorations — what is it?
Viscum album is a species of mistletoe in the family Santalaceae, commonly called European mistletoe, common mistletoe, or simply mistletoe (Old English mistle).
Native from Panama to southern Canada, this plant genus of 50 species belongs to the asparagus family alongside the agaves — name the genus?
Yucca (YUK-) is both the scientific name and common name for a genus native to North America from Panama to southern Canada.
This protrusion in the neck, formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx, becomes more prominent in most men during puberty — what is it?
Adam's apple: Feature of the neck. The Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.

This organic functional group, structured R−CH=O and alternatively called a formyl group when isolated from its side chain, appears throughout biologically and technologically important chemicals — what is it?
Aldehyde: Organic compound containing the functional group R–CH=O.
Sold under the brand name Norvasc, this long-acting calcium channel blocker treats high blood pressure and variant angina by relaxing and widening the arteries — what's the drug?
Amlodipine: Medication against high blood pressure.
Bridging biology and sociology, this scientific study of humanity has social, cultural, linguistic and biological branches, and treats archaeology as the study of the human past — what's the field?
Anthropology: Scientific study of humans, human behavior, and societies.
Unlike its counterpart which returns blood to the heart, this blood vessel usually carries oxygen-rich blood away from it — what is it?
Artery: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart.
This Indian jurist studied economics at Columbia and the London School of Economics before becoming the chief architect of his country's constitution. Who was he?
B. R. Ambedkar: Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer (1891–1956)
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and currants all fall under this small, pulpy, often brightly colored category of fruit — which Britain calls "soft fruit." What is it?
Berry: In the culinary sense, small edible fruit.
Launched in 1993 as a redesigned-wing, glass-cockpit upgrade of an earlier narrow-body jetliner series, this aircraft competes chiefly against the Airbus A320 family — which aircraft is it?
Boeing 737 Next Generation: Single-aisle airliner family.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways typically causes a cough lasting around three weeks and is usually caused by a virus?
Bronchitis: Inflammation of the large airways in the lungs.
Bearing distinctive fatty humps and used for milk, meat, and transport across deserts for millennia, which ungulate comes in a common one-humped form and a rarer two-humped form?
Its raw shell and seed are actually toxic until roasted or steamed, and the tropical American tree it grows on also yields a fleshy 'apple' — what is this familiar snack?
Cashew: Flowering plant in the family Anacardiaceae.
Released by OpenAI in November 2022 and built on generative pre-trained transformers, this chatbot is widely credited with setting off the current AI boom. Name it.

ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, originally released in November 2022, using large language models — specifically generative pre-trained transformers — and it accelerated the ongoing AI boom.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
Nicknamed the jade plant or money plant, this low-maintenance South African succulent thrives on neglect and barely any water — what's its botanical name?
Crassula ovata: Species of succulent. It is sometimes referred to as the money tree; however, Pachira aquatica also has this nickname.

Developed as a successor to an earlier delta-wing fighter family, this French all-weather interceptor entered service with the French Air Force in 1974, equipped with Cyrano IV radar — what aircraft is it?
Dassault Mirage F1: French attack aircraft. During the 1960s, Dassault commenced development of what would become the Mirage F1 as a private venture, alongside the larger Mirage F2.
Native to North Africa and West Asia, this annual herb in the celery family lends its leaves and seeds as both an herb and a spice — what is it?
Dill: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Derived from Greek words for 'brain' and 'suffering,' this umbrella medical term covers any disease or disorder that causes overall brain dysfunction — what is it?
Encephalopathy: Disorders or diseases of the brain.
Combining five of mathematics' most fundamental constants — e, i, pi, 1, and 0 — into a single elegant equation, this formula is often called the most beautiful in mathematics. What is it?
Euler's identity: Mathematical equation linking e, i and π.
This subfamily of cats, distinguished by a bony hyoid that lets its members purr instead of roar, is informally known as the small cats — which subfamily?
Felinae: Subfamily of Felidae. The Felinae or small cats are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

Present in about 80% of adults as harmless white or yellow bumps on the lips, cheeks, or gums, these visible sebaceous glands were first described in 1896 by an American dermatologist — what are they called?
Fordyce spots: Sebaceous glands that are present in most individuals.
Naming his most famous pistol after his 17th patent — not for holding seventeen rounds, as many assume — this Austrian engineer got his design into Austrian service in 1982 — who was he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland

The only Allied jet aircraft to see combat in World War II, this British fighter entered service with No. 616 Squadron RAF in July 1944, powered by engines pioneered by Frank Whittle — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor: Britain's first jet fighter, 1943–1980s.
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)
Native to Africa south of the Sahara, this domesticated bird has since been introduced everywhere from the West Indies to Australia — which species?
Helmeted guinea fowl: Species of bird. The helmeted guinea fowl (Numida meleagris) is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This psychiatric state brings a surge of energy, euphoria, and a reduced need for sleep — milder than its more severe cousin because it doesn't significantly impair daily functioning — what is it?
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
Son of Taiwanese immigrants, this engineer launched the world's most valuable company from a Denny's restaurant in 1993 after earning a Stanford master's degree — who is he?
Jensen Huang: Taiwanese and American businessman (born 1963)
Sometimes grown just for looks, this cabbage relative's leaves can be bumpy, curly, or flat, in colors from purple to green — what leafy vegetable is it?
Kale: Form of cabbage with green or purple leaves.
This is the most abundant genus of trees on Earth, dominating the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada despite dropping its needles every fall. What genus is it?
Larch: Genus of deciduous conifers in the family Pinaceae.
Syntax, semantics, morphology, phonetics, phonology, and pragmatics are all branches of which scientific field?
This American experimental physicist won the 1968 Nobel Prize for discovering resonance states using the hydrogen bubble chamber — who was he?
Luis Walter Alvarez: American physicist, inventor and professor (1911–1988)

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
Native to Indomalaya and Australasia, this deciduous member of the mahogany family goes by names like chinaberry tree and Persian lilac — what is it?

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.
Nicknamed noni, this pungent-smelling fruit tree in the coffee family was spread across the Pacific by Polynesian sailors and is now used mainly in traditional medicine and juices — which plant?
Morinda citrifolia: Species of plant. It is commonly known as noni or Indian mulberry, among many other names.
Made of two fused benzene rings, this pungent white crystalline compound is the main ingredient in traditional mothballs — what is it?
Naphthalene: Chemical compound. It is a white crystalline solid with a characteristic odor that is detectable at concentrations as low as 0.08 ppm.
Unlike its more predictably spreading cousin, this group of blood cancers can appear in multiple parts of the body at once and cause enlarged lymph nodes, fevers, and night sweats — which condition?
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of cancer of lymph nodes.

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
From a single western-Mediterranean flowering plant come both a notorious drug and the tiny dark seeds sprinkled on your bagel — which species is it?
Papaver somniferum: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
Known for its speed, this large crow-sized raptor has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts, and a black head — an avivore with marked sexual dimorphism — what is it?
Peregrine falcon: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.
Flagged by the WHO as one of the greatest antibiotic-resistance threats to humans, this rod-shaped bacterium causes hospital infections like ventilator-associated pneumonia — which pathogen?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Species of bacterium. P. aeruginosa is able to selectively inhibit various antibiotics from penetrating its outer membrane and has high resistance to several antibiotics.
Named for the ragged look of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants causes up to half of all pollen-related allergy cases despite a genus name meaning 'food of the gods' — which plant?
Ragweed: Genus of plants. The name "ragweed" is derived from "ragged" + "weed," coming from the ragged appearance of the plant's leaves.
Also called vitamin B2, this nutrient forms two key coenzymes for energy metabolism, can be prescribed for corneal thinning, and taken orally may cut down migraines in adults — which vitamin is it?
Riboflavin: Vitamin, dietary supplement, and yellow food dye.

Built by a Swedish manufacturer, this single-engine fighter was the first mass-produced canard-design aircraft and the first with a digital avionics computer, unsurpassed until the Tornado arrived in 1981 — which jet?
Saab 37 Viggen: 1967 Swedish fighter aircraft family.
Distinguished from true seals by external ear flaps and the ability to walk on all fours, these marine mammals include a giant subspecies that can weigh up to 1,000 kilograms. What are they?
Sea lion: Subfamily of aquatic mammals.

No metal beats this one for electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, or reflectivity, and it's mostly mined as a byproduct of refining copper, gold, lead, and zinc — which element, symbol Ag, is it?
Silver: Chemical element with atomic number 47 (Ag)
Combining vowel and consonant sounds into words for acts like persuading or declaring, this use of the human voice can even happen without any listener at all — what is it?
Speech: Human vocal communication using spoken language.
A bitter, colorless alkaloid from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, it kills birds and rodents by triggering muscular convulsions and asphyxia. Which poison is it?
Strychnine: Poisonous substance used as pesticide.
Named after a figure from Greek mythology, this blue-gray transition metal with atomic number 73 is prized for corrosion resistance and shows up in capacitors inside computers. What element is this?
Tantalum: Chemical element with atomic number 73 (Ta)
Covered in sharp spikes along its leaf margins to ward off herbivores, this prickly flowering plant's fluffy seed head is known as 'down.' What is it?
Thistle: Common name of a group of flowering plants.
Sold as Tramal, this opioid painkiller doubles as an SNRI — which means it carries a rare risk of serotonin syndrome. What is it?
This hypothetical element 126, nicknamed eka-plutonium, intrigues physicists because 126 may be a 'magic number' of protons sitting near the center of a predicted island of stability — what is it?
Unbihexium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 126 (Ubh)
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
Nominated by Einstein, this Austrian physicist won the 1945 Nobel Prize for describing the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the tiny neutral particle later named the neutrino — who is he?
The symbol for niobium is Nb. Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb and atomic number 41.
The symbol for holmium is Ho. Holmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ho and atomic number 67.

In what year was Kirk Douglas born?
Kirk Douglas (born Issur Danielovitch; December 9, 1916 – February 5, 2020) was an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Kirstie Alley born?
Kirstie Alley: Kirstie Louise Alley (January 12, 1951 – December 5, 2022) was an American actress.
In what year was Samuel L. Jackson born?
Samuel L. Jackson: Samuel Leroy Jackson (born December 21, 1948) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Guy Ritchie born?
Guy Ritchie: Guy Stuart Ritchie (born 10 September 1968) is an English filmmaker known primarily for British comedy gangster films and large-scale action-adventure films.

Florence Pugh ( PEW; born 3 January 1996) is an English actress.

Bryan Cranston: Bryan Lee Cranston (born March 7, 1956) is an American actor and filmmaker.

Mads Mikkelsen: Mads Dittmann Mikkelsen (Danish: [ˈmæs ditsʰmɛːn ˈme̝kl̩sn̩]; born 22 November 1965) is a Danish actor.
In what year was Treat Williams born?
Treat Williams: Richard Treat Williams Jr. (December 1, 1951 – June 12, 2023) was an American actor, whose career on stage and in film and television spanned five decades.
In what year was Demi Moore born?
Demi Moore: Demi Gene Moore ( də-MEE; née Guynes; born November 11, 1962) is an American actress and producer.

M. Night Shyamalan: Night" Shyamalan ( SHAH-mə-lahn; born August 6, 1970) is an American filmmaker.

Kirsten Dunst: Kirsten Caroline Dunst ( KEER-stən; born April 30, 1982) is an American actress.

Maggie Smith: Dame Margaret Natalie Smith (28 December 1934 – 27 September 2024) was a British actress.

Cameron Boyce: Cameron Mica Boyce (May 28, 1999 – July 6, 2019) was an American actor.

Boston Strangler is a 2023 American historical crime drama film written and directed by Matt Ruskin.

Gran Turismo is a 2023 American biographical sports drama film based on the sim racing video game series developed by Polyphony Digital.
In what year was Hellraiser first released?
Hellraiser is a 1987 British supernatural horror film written and directed by Clive Barker in his directorial debut.
In what year was The Maze Runner first released?
